Army Black Knights.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Jeff Monken beginning his 13th year at Army and makes the tenure point vividly: setting aside UTSA's Jeff Traylor, his 12 years nearly equal the rest of the conference's head coaches combined.
Army Black Knights.dc: Daryl Dixon, promoted from pass game coordinator after Nate Woody left for Cincinnati.
Army Black Knights.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Army Black Knights.dc_status: New — the guide records Nate Woody's move to Cincinnati and Dixon's promotion, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Army Black Knights.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Army Black Knights.offensive_scheme: Addressed by its consequences rather than by name — the guide's option-based framing runs through the run volume, noting Army was outgained in conference play partly because of how much they run relative to opponents, and recording the fall from 5.7 yards per carry in 2024 conference games to 4.38 in 2025.
Army Black Knights.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Army as almost always undersized in the trenches but usually experienced, and this season as an exception.
Army Black Knights.run_pass: Heavily run-weighted as a stated characteristic: the guide notes Cale Hellums carried 304 times for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns while adding four passing scores and 694 yards, and that Army's style limits turnover volume.
Army Black Knights.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's quarterback concern is workload — 304 carries is a brutal load for a 5-foot-10 player and must be factored into any long-term position on Army — and it allows Monken and coordinator Cody Worley may have found something in converted quarterback Godspower Nwawuihe.
Army Black Knights.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes but is promoted from within. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 13.
Army Black Knights.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator, and mitigated by continuity of knowledge: the guide notes Dixon has been with the programme for ten seasons so he knows the scheme and the player types, while adding that he is mostly a defensive backs coach.
Army Black Knights.prior_school: Cincinnati is where Nate Woody went. The rest is internal — Dixon's ten seasons at Army.
Army Black Knights.vsin_assessment: Solidity credited, with a specific downward trend flagged. The guide reads a 7-6 winning record as further evidence of how solid Monken has been, given repeating 12-2 was always going to be insurmountable and the losses of Bryson Daily and Kanye Udoh. Its core statistical argument is a reversal: Army was outgained by nearly a full yard per play in conference play, having outgained conference foes by nearly 1.2 yards per play in 2024. It also draws a precise historical parallel — Navy joined the AAC in 2015, went 7-1 in league play in each of its first two seasons, then fell to 4-4 in year three and 2-6 in year four — against Army's own 8-0 then 4-4.
Army Black Knights.strengths: By far the longest tenure in the conference, offensive-coordinator continuity, a returning quarterback with 18 rushing touchdowns, a defensive coordinator promoted after ten seasons in the programme, and a +12 turnover margin across two years of conference play.
Army Black Knights.concerns: A conference yards-per-play advantage that flipped from +1.2 to nearly -1.0 in a year, a quarterback carrying nearly 41% of the team's rushes with everyone who shared the load gone, all of the top seven tacklers departed, and only 15 sacks generated.
Army Black Knights.betting: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The coaching-linked reasons are stated directly: a Hellums injury would be brutal since there is no game experience behind him, and losing Nate Woody hurts the defense.

Charlotte 49ers.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records Tim Albin having three straight double-digit winning seasons at Ohio before leaving for Charlotte, and notes he primarily coached offensive linemen and running backs before becoming Ohio's coordinator.
Charlotte 49ers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Charlotte 49ers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Charlotte 49ers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Charlotte 49ers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Charlotte 49ers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Charlotte 49ers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records 2.7 yards per carry and 4.6 yards per play.
Charlotte 49ers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's verdict on the room is blunt — none of the options are particularly good — and it records Conner Harrell, probably the best quarterback on the roster, being out until around mid-October.
Charlotte 49ers.continuity: Complete as printed. The Stability Score table (p. 42) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 1 for 9 returning starters — totalling 15, against a 1-11 record.
Charlotte 49ers.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Charlotte 49ers.prior_school: Ohio for Albin. On the roster the guide records Grayson Loftis from Duke, Conner Harrell from North Carolina and Cole Gonzales from Western Carolina.
Charlotte 49ers.portal_recruiting: Assessed deliberately modestly. The guide says neither the incoming class nor the portal class graded highly for 247Sports relative to the conference, but there are many more bodies and some are probably better at football than what was there. It records that Charlotte's boosters did fund a real attempt at quarterback last season.
Charlotte 49ers.vsin_assessment: The job rated harder than the coach. The guide says Albin left a good job at Ohio for what it calls arguably the biggest challenge in the American, rating Charlotte probably the second-toughest job behind Rice — though it notes results point to Charlotte as the toughest. It attributes much of the collapse to how painfully thin the roster was when Albin arrived, and identifies a multi-year structural problem: Charlotte is not big or strong enough up front, with a -2.3 yards-per-carry differential last year and -1.6 the year before, against a positive differential for the 2019 bowl team. It observes that Albin primarily coached offensive linemen and running backs, and that the athletic department showed the same instinct when hiring Biff Poggi over trench toughness.
Charlotte 49ers.strengths: A head coach with three straight double-digit winning seasons at his previous stop whose own coaching background is in the trenches — which the guide identifies as exactly the programme's structural weakness — full staff continuity per the Stability Score table, and many more bodies on the roster.
Charlotte 49ers.concerns: A 1-11 season with 14.3 points scored and more than 36 allowed per game, being outgained by nearly two yards per play, no conference loss closer than 11 points, 14 sacks, 2.7 yards per carry, a quarterback room the guide calls not particularly good with the best option out until mid-October, and portal and recruiting classes that did not grade highly.
Charlotte 49ers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its projection is 1.81 wins, and its coaching-linked conclusion is conditional: improving up front is how Albin finds momentum.

East Carolina Pirates.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Blake Harrell at 14-5, having won five of the final six in 2024 and gone 9-4 last season, and describes him as 46 years old and able to take a big defensive coordinator job or a bigger head coaching role.
East Carolina Pirates.oc: Jordan Davis, who worked under Eric Morris at North Texas.
East Carolina Pirates.dc: Not addressed by name for 2026. The guide records that Josh Aldridge ran the defense with Harrell last season and that both previous coordinators left, for Ole Miss and South Florida.
East Carolina Pirates.oc_status: New — the guide records Harrell working with two new coordinators after his previous ones left for Ole Miss and South Florida, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
East Carolina Pirates.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator, and the guide notes Harrell is starting from scratch again with a new coordinator.
East Carolina Pirates.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
East Carolina Pirates.offensive_scheme: Named by lineage and then carefully corrected. The guide records Jordan Davis bringing a scheme change from Eric Morris's North Texas offense, which led the nation in scoring at over 45 points and in yards at just over 512 per game while ranking third in yards per play — then corrects a likely assumption with data: a Morris offense is not merely a chuck-it attack, since Drew Mestemaker threw 463 times for nearly 4,400 yards while Caleb Hawkins carried 231 times for 1,434 yards on 517 team rushing attempts.
East Carolina Pirates.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Harrell and Josh Aldridge producing 20.1 points and just over 5.1 yards per play allowed with only two returning starters, improving against the run, generating more sacks and forcing 24 takeaways for a +10 turnover margin.
East Carolina Pirates.run_pass: Addressed through the incoming scheme's actual balance, and the guide sees a good chance of run-game recovery after East Carolina fell from 4.8 to 4.1 yards per carry.
East Carolina Pirates.qb_development: Addressed as a portal skill rather than a development record. The guide notes Katin Houser, another Harrell portal find, was very solid last season and credits Harrell with a finger on the pulse of free agency, then weighs Miami transfer Emory Williams — bigger and more athletic — against four-time transfer Mitch Griffis, closer to Mestemaker's skill set though lacking his size.
East Carolina Pirates.continuity: Only the head coach returns. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 7 returning starters, totalling 4.
East Carolina Pirates.staff_turnover: Both coordinators left in one offseason, for Ole Miss and South Florida, and the guide records Harrell working with two new ones.
East Carolina Pirates.prior_school: North Texas for Jordan Davis, and the connection reaches the roster: he brought backup back Ashton Gray and receiver Landon Sides, so some players know the scheme. The guide also records Emory Williams from Miami and Mitch Griffis from Texas Tech.
East Carolina Pirates.portal_recruiting: Credited to the head coach — the guide says Harrell has a finger on the pulse of free agency, citing the earlier Katin Houser find.
East Carolina Pirates.vsin_assessment: Success framed as bittersweet, with a caveat the guide supplies against its own numbers. It openly wonders whether this is Harrell's last season, and says repeating would be thoroughly impressive with virtually none of last season's major contributors back and two new coordinators. Its own caveat is precise: East Carolina allowed just 390 yards combined in wins over Campbell and Coastal Carolina, and 71 rushing yards on 53 carries, so the conference numbers were not as strong as the full-season figures suggest — balanced by the Pirates still outgaining American opponents by 0.65 yards per play as the offense strengthened through the season.
East Carolina Pirates.strengths: A head coach at 14-5 who the guide expects to attract bigger jobs, a documented defensive rebuild from only two returning starters, an offensive coordinator from the nation's highest-scoring offense who brought players who already know the scheme, and portal instincts the guide credits explicitly.
East Carolina Pirates.concerns: A Stability Score of 4 with only seven returning starters, both coordinators lost in one offseason, no established quarterback, a possibly shaky offensive line early, and a head coach the guide expects may not stay.
East Carolina Pirates.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Florida Atlantic Owls.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records that Zach Kittley is the youngest head coach in FBS and that he did double duty as coordinator in his first head-coaching year.
Florida Atlantic Owls.oc: Zach Kittley himself in year one; the guide records he did double duty as coordinator.
Florida Atlantic Owls.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Florida Atlantic Owls.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Florida Atlantic Owls.play_caller: Zach Kittley, who the guide records doing double duty as coordinator in his first head-coaching year, with the consequence that he has had far more time to evaluate fits this time.
Florida Atlantic Owls.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide calls Kittley a big Air Raid proponent and expects another high-variance team given heavy pass volume.
Florida Atlantic Owls.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide calls the defensive line objectively terrible, with American opponents averaging 232 rushing yards per game.
Florida Atlantic Owls.tempo: Not addressed directly. The guide's characterisation is heavy pass volume rather than pace.
Florida Atlantic Owls.run_pass: Sharply pass-weighted, and the guide treats the imbalance as a problem. It calls the rushing numbers laughable — 105 yards per game at 3.5 per carry, falling to 82 yards and 2.9 in American play — notes this is not a conference known for physical defenses so there were no holes at all, and offers a possible explanation in the line shifting to a very pass-heavy blocking scheme.
Florida Atlantic Owls.qb_development: Addressed as a shared responsibility. The guide defends Caden Veltkamp partially — he was asked to throw a lot and Florida Atlantic trailed often, so the 17 interceptions may not all be his, especially given he had only 11 in three seasons at Western Kentucky — and identifies the structural problem as Easton Messer still being the only true go-to target.
Florida Atlantic Owls.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 42) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 2 for 12 returning starters — totalling 16.
Florida Atlantic Owls.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Florida Atlantic Owls.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Drew Devillier from Rice and Leonard Farrow from Fairmont State by the junior college route.
Florida Atlantic Owls.portal_recruiting: Substantial and targeted. In a conference the guide says is badly short of returning starters, Kittley has a couple of handfuls plus 30 portal additions including defenders capable of creating negative plays, and the guide records that he and his staff hammered the defensive side in the portal, mixing year-two scheme players with newcomers, with the line and front seven clear focal points.
Florida Atlantic Owls.vsin_assessment: Belief in the coach's trajectory, stated with unusual precision about conviction. The guide sees the makings of a good team despite a 4-8 finish and a sixth straight season short of six wins, with Kittley's plan visibly in motion, and says he has risen rapidly for a reason. It divides responsibility for the -21 turnover margin rather than blaming one player — Veltkamp threw 17 interceptions, but Brett Dewhurst's defense forced only eight turnovers. It is explicit that this is not a strong opinion but a lean: a 4-8 team with a -21 turnover margin now has more talent in year two of the system, and Kittley has had far more time to evaluate fits. Projection is 5.64 wins.
Florida Atlantic Owls.strengths: A Stability Score of 16 with everything returning, year two of a defined system under a head coach the guide says has risen rapidly for a reason, 30 portal additions concentrated on the defensive front, a 104-catch receiver, and a running back room the guide finds intriguing.
Florida Atlantic Owls.concerns: A -21 turnover margin split between a quarterback with 17 interceptions and a defense that forced eight, a rushing attack the guide calls laughable, a defensive line it calls objectively terrible against a 150-yard rushing differential across eight conference games, and only one true go-to receiving target.
Florida Atlantic Owls.betting: The guide's lean is argued directly from the coaching situation: a 4-8 team with a -21 turnover margin now has more talent in year two of the system, and Kittley — who did double duty as coordinator in his first head-coaching year — has had far more time to evaluate fits.

Memphis Tigers.previous_hc_experience: Extensive, and set out in full by the Coaching Carousel. It records that Charles Huff seemed like a bit of an odd hire at Marshall, having primarily served as a running backs coach in his career, but was on Nick Saban's staff when the Thundering Herd came calling; that after a 32-20 run in Huntington he went to Southern Miss because Marshall let the reigning Sun Belt champion head coach walk away; and that he took a big chunk of his roster there and went 7-5 before leveling up to Memphis.
Memphis Tigers.oc: Kevin Decker, in from Old Dominion.
Memphis Tigers.dc: Lance Guidry, who worked with Huff at Marshall.
Memphis Tigers.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Memphis Tigers.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Memphis Tigers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Memphis Tigers.offensive_scheme: Described precisely rather than named. The guide characterises Decker's philosophy as high-octane and explosive, but starting with the ground game with the pass coming off it — Old Dominion averaged 5.6 yards per carry and nearly 240 rushing yards, ranked top-20 in yards per play at 32 points per game, and his 2021 Fordham offense averaged over 600 yards per game.
Memphis Tigers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Memphis Tigers.tempo: Raised conditionally — the guide says the roster could make for a fun offense if Decker plays with tempo.
Memphis Tigers.run_pass: Stated: the ground game comes first, with the pass coming off it.
Memphis Tigers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records no established starter among Marcus Stokes, a multi-year West Florida starter, Air Noland, a highly touted recruit who never played at Ohio State before transferring to South Carolina, and Huff recruit Denzel Gardner.
Memphis Tigers.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 2.
Memphis Tigers.staff_turnover: Complete, following Ryan Silverfield's departure for Arkansas and a mass player exodus. The guide records this as essentially a brand-new roster for Huff.
Memphis Tigers.prior_school: Marshall for Lance Guidry, whom Huff worked with there; Old Dominion for Kevin Decker; Southern Miss for a group of players who followed Huff, including J'Mond Tapp with 7.5 sacks plus Ian Foster and Anthony Richard, who each had 10 pass breakups. The guide also records Dallan Hayden from Ohio State by way of Colorado, Jaylin Carter from Southern Miss and Manny Covey from Cincinnati.
Memphis Tigers.portal_recruiting: The whole roster, and the guide reads it as a coherent philosophy rather than a random collection: noteworthy recruits who could not crack lineups elsewhere, all carrying chips on their shoulders. The Coaching Carousel adds the resource point — Memphis has a pretty robust NIL budget thanks to FedEx, and Huff, who has connections all over the country from his different stops, could find immediate and prolonged success with resources he did not have at his two previous stops.
Memphis Tigers.vsin_assessment: A clear bet on the coach. The team pages judge Huff an outstanding coach on the evidence so far, concede new schemes and heavy transfer volume may take a year, credit two good coordinator hires and a sense that he has motivated players discarded or cast off elsewhere, and close on pedigree — he has worked under James Franklin and Nick Saban and knows how to identify talent. The Coaching Carousel notes Marshall let a reigning Sun Belt champion walk away and expects the NIL resources at Memphis to matter.
Memphis Tigers.strengths: A head coach with a 32-20 run at Marshall and a Sun Belt title, worked under Nick Saban and James Franklin, two coordinator hires the guide rates — one with a top-20 yards-per-play offense, the other a really good hire he already knows — nationwide connections, and a robust NIL budget he has not previously had.
Memphis Tigers.concerns: A Stability Score of 2 with an essentially brand-new roster, no truly established skill players, new schemes on both sides that the guide concedes may take a year, and a defense whose upside it rates lower than the offense's because there are fewer noteworthy recruits on that side.
Memphis Tigers.betting: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, stated explicitly as a bet on the coach — two good coordinator hires, and a sense Huff has motivated players discarded or cast off elsewhere. Projection is 7.38 wins.
Memphis Tigers.carousel_summary: Adam Burke calls this an interesting season for Huff and traces the whole path. He seemed like a bit of an odd hire at Marshall, having primarily served as a running backs coach in his career, but he was on Nick Saban's staff when the Thundering Herd came calling. After a 32-20 run in Huntington he went to Southern Miss because Marshall let the reigning Sun Belt Conference champion head coach walk away; he took a big chunk of his roster with him and went 7-5 before leveling up to Memphis. Burke then turns to resources: Memphis has a pretty robust NIL budget thanks to FedEx, and Huff, who has connections all over the country from his different stops, could find immediate and prolonged success with resources he did not have at his two previous stops.
